The cellular involution gives $G_\lambda(s,t)=G_\lambda(t,s)$. Associativity of the threefold product yields $\langle xa,y\rangle=\langle x,ya^*\rangle$, since both sides compute the coefficient in the cell layer of the same product. [F1, algebra]

Cell purity. Let $z$ be a central idempotent of $A$. On the cell layer $J_\lambda\cong C_\lambda^*\otimes_FC_\lambda$ the equality of left and right multiplication by $z$ gives $B\otimes\operatorname{Id}=\operatorname{Id}\otimes A_\lambda$ for the first- and second-factor coefficient matrices; comparing matrix coefficients shows every off-diagonal entry of $B$ and $A_\lambda$ vanishes and all diagonal entries of $B$ and $A_\lambda$ are equal, so both are a single scalar $\theta_\lambda$ times the identity. Since $z$ is idempotent, $\theta_\lambda\in\{0,1\}$. Applying this to all primitive central idempotents, whose sum is $1$, exactly one acts as $1$ on the nonzero cell module $C_\lambda$ and the others as $0$; hence $C_\lambda$, and therefore every composition factor of it, lies in one block. Nonzero form gives a simple head. Let $R_\lambda:=\{x\in C_\lambda:\langle x,C_\lambda\rangle=0\}$ be the radical of the form.
